newsitem.title: NORWAY: RISING CYCLICAL STOCKS SUPPORT NORWEGIAN SHARES.
newsitem.headline: RISING CYCLICAL STOCKS SUPPORT NORWEGIAN SHARES.

text.p: Norwegian shares held in marginal positive territory on Tuesday and dealers said the market was showing fundamental strength with interest in cyclic stocks.
"The strength in the Norwegian market is because it is geared to cyclic stocks and not so very dependent on interest rates," said one broker. "And the cyclical stocks are rising."
Oslo's Total share index edged forward 0.37 percent to close the session at 1324.12 points in turnover of 1.1 billion crowns.
Norwegian Seafoods ASA, the world's largest catcher and processor of white fish, dropped 20 percent to end at 39.90 crowns after posting a surprise pre-tax loss in the first half.
The company, 60 percent owned by Aker RGI ASA, attributed the loss to a 400 million crown restructuring cost.
Anglo-Norwegian Kvaerner ASA continued to make good ground, closing 2.46 percent up in the A share at 478.50 crowns. Turnover was 69 million crowns.
Dealers said Kvaerner's hefty advance this week - 20.5 crowns since Friday's close -- came after it announced it would merge all its Norwegian offshore divisions.
"The share is up partly on speculation that they will merge and then be spun off as a separate listed company, but mainly on expectations that it will add value," said another dealer.
